title: Your First Weekend at Illinois Wesleyan University, Shared as Cards
description: A practical, under-21-safe sequence for learning the campus, finding student resources, and exploring two public Bloomington destinations.

cards.title: Start at the student center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Get oriented
cards.notes: Locate the information desk, Student Involvement office, bookstore, and Tommy’s so you know where to return for help and events.
cards.short_summary: Use Hansen as your first reference point for campus services and involvement.
cards.evidence_claim: Hansen Student Center houses an information desk, bookstore, Tommy’s dining, Student Involvement, student organizations, and meeting spaces.
cards.access_notes: During fall and spring classes, the building lists Friday hours of 7:30 a.m.–10 p.m. and weekend hours of 10 a.m.–10 p.m.; summer weekends are closed.

cards.title: Learn the center of campus
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Walk the main quad
cards.notes: Cross Eckley Quadrangle and identify the surrounding landmarks now; it will make later walks between campus buildings easier.
cards.short_summary: Build a mental map by walking IWU’s named main quadrangle.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU’s current campus map names Eckley Quadrangle, and the student-organization handbook identifies it as the Main Quad.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus location; check campus notices and posted restrictions before visiting.

cards.title: Set up your study anchor
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Find academic support
cards.notes: Step inside, locate the service desk, and note where the Writing Center, technology help, and other learning-support units are based.
cards.short_summary: Find the library services and campus partners you may need once classes begin.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ames Library provides research services and houses the Writing Center, Information Technology Services, and other student-support units.
cards.source_title: The Ames Library – Faculty & Staff Directory
cards.access_notes: Regular fall and spring hours are Friday 7:45 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m., and Sunday noon–8 p.m.; orientation and break schedules differ.

cards.title: Make an art stop
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · See the current exhibition
cards.notes: Enter through the Ames School of Art and Design, check the posted exhibition information, and spend a focused half hour with the work.
cards.short_summary: Add a free contemporary-art visit to your first campus circuit.
cards.evidence_claim: The Merwin and Wakeley Galleries present contemporary art exhibitions and state that exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Friday noon–4 p.m., Tuesday 7–9 p.m., and Saturday–Sunday 1–4 p.m.; verify the current exhibition calendar.

cards.title: Pause downtown
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Choose your own order
cards.notes: Use the official menu or ordering app if you want something, then orient yourself on North Main Street before continuing downtown.
cards.short_summary: Begin Saturday at a named all-ages café in Downtown Bloomington.
cards.evidence_claim: The Coffee Hound’s official locations page lists its Downtown Bloomington café at 407 N. Main Street and daily hours of 6:30 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The business currently lists daily hours of 6:30 a.m.–4 p.m.; confirm before departing because business hours can change.

cards.title: Meet Bloomington through its history
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Explore the courthouse museum
cards.notes: Enter from Washington Street and choose one of the permanent galleries as your starting point rather than trying to cover all four floors.
cards.short_summary: Connect your new campus town to the people and events preserved by its history museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum occupies four floors, offers five permanent exhibits and a Discovery Room, and grants free admission to students and children.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Saturday hours of 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and directs visitors to its Washington Street entrance at 200 N. Main Street.

cards.title: Return for a garden reset
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Walk a campus growing space
cards.notes: Follow the campus map to the Peace Garden, observe what is growing, and leave beds and greenhouse areas undisturbed unless invited to help.
cards.short_summary: See how a named campus garden connects food, learning, and civic engagement.
cards.evidence_claim: The IWU Peace Garden serves students’ curricular and culinary needs and supports civic engagement and food-growing partnerships.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden conditions and organized work opportunities vary; follow posted guidance and do not enter restricted growing areas.

cards.title: Find the recreation hub
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Scope out future workouts
cards.notes: Walk through only where student access permits, note the recreation and fitness areas, and check posted schedules before planning a workout.
cards.short_summary: Learn where IWU students go for indoor recreation, fitness, and athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: The Shirk Center is used by students for fitness and recreation and includes multi-use courts, a 200-meter track, and fitness facilities.
cards.source_title: IWU’s Shirk Center Celebrating 30 Years of Athletics, Community
cards.access_notes: Student entry and facility availability depend on identification requirements, posted schedules, team use, and events; verify before exercising.

cards.title: Take a daylight trail walk
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Explore a short segment
cards.notes: Choose a signed trailhead, keep right, stay aware at crossings, and turn back while you still have ample daylight for the return trip.
cards.short_summary: Use a manageable walk to see part of Bloomington-Normal beyond campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Constitution Trail is a public multi-segment trail system connecting Bloomington and Normal, with mapped trailheads and recreation rules.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from one hour before sunrise until one hour after sunset. Keep right, obey signs, and use designated access points and crossings.

cards.title: Close with a quiet check-in
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Study, reflect, or talk
cards.notes: Visit the open common spaces for a brief reset, and note the Multifaith Engagement office as a resource for future questions or programs.
cards.short_summary: End the weekend in an inclusive campus space for reflection and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Evelyn Chapel houses the Office of Multifaith Engagement and provides spaces to study, converse, and prepare complimentary hot drinks.
cards.access_notes: The university currently states that Evelyn Chapel is open seven days a week from 8 a.m.–11 p.m.; scheduled programs may affect individual spaces.

warnings: Business, facility, exhibition, and academic-calendar hours can change; consult the linked direct pages and posted notices before visiting.
Coordinates and map URLs are null because they were not independently verified from direct authoritative pages during this pass.
